interpretation.selection: For each of the review-roster users (U100,U101,U102), their profile-shown workspace membership (user_teams), kept only if that workspace's audit-log channel (C1/C2/C3) contains a message reacted to by a user whose real_name is 'Alex'. The intended focal condition binds REACTION.user_id -> USER.real_name, distinguishing reactor identity from mere message authorship.

checks.name: prompt_path_fidelity
checks.evidence: Route WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP->WORKSPACE->CONVERSATION->MESSAGE->REACTION->USER with focal field users.real_name at node 5 matches the request's 'reacted to by someone named Alex' — the reactor's identity, not the author's. Auxiliary channel-ID restriction (C1,C2,C3) is preserved.

checks.name: resolution
checks.evidence: The underspecified card treats two users as equally valid matches for 'named Alex': U200 'Alex Rivera' (clean first-name match, reacts on M1/C1) and U201 'Alexandra Cho' (substring-only match on 'alex' inside 'Alexandra', reacts on M3/C2). However U201's seeded display_name is 'Ali', not 'Alex', which undercuts the claim that she would ordinarily be referred to as 'Alex'. A third real 'Alex' (U202 Alex Turner, exact first-name match) never reacts, so he correctly plays no role here, but his existence highlights that the constructed ambiguity relies on a weaker substring match (Alexandra) rather than a second genuine 'Alex' identity. Whether a reasonable reader would accept Alexandra Cho as satisfying 'someone named Alex' is a genuine semantic judgment call, not a clear pass or fail.

checks.name: negatives
checks.evidence: U102/T3 is a legitimate near-miss: C3 has a message (M5) authored by 'Alex Turner' (right person, wrong role — author not reactor) and the only reaction on C3 (M6) is by 'Jordan Lee' (U203), who is not named Alex. This satisfies the auxiliary channel/message condition but fails the focal reaction-by-Alex condition under every interpretation, exactly as claimed.

checks.name: realism_and_hints
checks.evidence: IDs (U100-U102 roster, T1-T3 workspaces, C1-C3 channels) are simple and do not encode the answer beyond ordinary mapping; message texts and real names are ordinary and do not telegraph the focal distinction. No degenerate early anchors.

checks.name: api_scope
checks.evidence: Actor U900 is an admin of T1/T2/T3 and a member of C1/C2/C3, satisfying conversations.history and reactions.get access. users.info exposes one workspace per queried roster user per the runtime qualification (U100/T1, U101/T2, U102/T3 each hold exactly one user_teams row), supporting a reproducible 'profile-shown workspace' read. Reactor identification proceeds via reactions.get (returns user_id) then users.info per ID, consistent with the stated constraint that users.info cannot search by name.

checks.name: cards_and_spec
checks.evidence: Card fields match the locked schema; Referent set for the underspecified case uses selection/partial_constraints/candidate_sets exactly per convention, with Alternative sufficient identifying sets correctly left null. Task spec line 1 preserves the requested action, roster IDs, channel IDs, and the 'reacted to by Alex' condition verbatim in substance.

checks.name: mutation_integrity
checks.evidence: Clean-generation seed matches the declared assignment: only two reactions (M1/U200, M3/U201) among substring-'alex' users occur on in-scope audit channels, exactly reproducing the declared two disjoint candidate sets ({U100,T1} and {U101,T2}) and the one near-miss ({U102,T3}); no unintended extra 'Alex' reactor or workspace match exists in the seed (U202 Alex Turner never reacts).

issues: The second candidate set (U101/T2 via 'Alexandra Cho') rests on a bare substring match ('alex' inside 'Alexandra') that conflicts with her own seeded display_name 'Ali', making it uncertain whether a reasonable reader would treat her as 'someone named Alex' rather than treating only U200 (and the non-reacting U202) as genuine 'Alex' matches. This should be confirmed or the ambiguity re-grounded with two unambiguous 'Alex' identities before the underspecified resolution is certified.
